content: 1. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, the venetoclax dose should be reduced by at least 50%, and patients should be closely monitored for signs of venetoclax toxicities. 2. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of venlafaxine by altering hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 3. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of verapamil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, cobicistat also increases verapamil levels through the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of inhaled vilanterol/fluticasone furoate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. In serious cases, alternative drugs should be considered. 5. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate through CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used due to the potential for serious adverse effects. 6. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases vilazodone levels through the same mechanism. If intolerable adverse effects occur, the daily dose of vilazodone should be reduced to 20 mg. Close monitoring is required. 7. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Temporary withholding of the antiretroviral regimen may be considered in patients with significant side effects. If prolonged withholding is necessary, a revised regimen without CYP3A or P-gp inhibitors should be initiated. 8. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vinblastine through CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Similar to darunavir, consider withholding the antiretroviral regimen if significant adverse effects occur. 9. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vincristine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients should be monitored for hematologic or gastrointestinal adverse effects. Temporary withholding of the antiretroviral regimen may be necessary in cases of significant side effects. If prolonged withholding is required, a revised regimen without CYP3A or P-gp inhibitors should be considered. 10. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vincristine through CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Similar to darunavir, consider withholding the antiretroviral regimen if significant adverse effects occur. 11. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of liposomal vincristine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases liposomal vincristine levels through the same mechanism. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 12. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases vinorelbine levels through the same mechanism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown, but caution and monitoring are advised. 13. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases voclosporin levels through the same mechanism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Darunavir also increases vorapaxar levels through the same mechanism. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. Close monitoring is required. 15. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Voriconazole also increases darunavir levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. In serious cases, alternative drugs should be considered. 16. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of vortioxetine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. 17. Darunavir may alter warfarin serum concentrations, either increasing or decreasing them. Cobicistat may also increase warfarin levels through mechanisms involving CYP3A4 and other enzymes. Frequent INR monitoring and warfarin dose adjustments are recommended. 18. Zafirlukast increases darunavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Darunavir increases zaleplon levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 20. Darunavir increases zanubrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases zanubrutinib levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Zanubrutinib doses should be reduced to 80 mg once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, the previous zanubrutinib dose should be resumed. 21. Darunavir increases zileuton levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. 22. Darunavir increases ziprasidone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 23. Darunavir increases zolpidem levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases zolpidem levels through the same mechanism. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 24. Darunavir increases zonisamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 25. Darunavir increases zuranolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Cobicistat also increases zuranolone levels through the same mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Zuranolone doses should be reduced when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 26. Common adverse effects of darunavir/cobicistat include nausea, diarrhea, headache, rash, abdominal pain, vomiting, and anorexia. Laboratory abnormalities include elevated triglycerides, increased creatine kinase, elevated liver enzymes (ALT/AST), and glycosuria. Serious adverse effects include rhabdomyolysis, toxic epidermal necrolysis, and immune reconstitution syndrome. 27. Darunavir and cobicistat are secreted into the milk of lactating rats. Due to the potential for HIV transmission, viral resistance, and serious adverse reactions in breastfed infants, mothers receiving this therapy should not breastfeed. 28. Darunavir/cobicistat should be taken with food to improve absorption. Darunavir is extensively metabolized by CYP3A enzymes, while cobicistat is metabolized by CYP3A and CYP2D6 enzymes. Both drugs are highly protein-bound, and their half-lives are approximately 7 hours (darunavir) and 4 hours (cobicistat). 29. HIV genotypic testing is recommended for antiretroviral treatment-experienced patients. If genotypic testing is not feasible, darunavir/cobicistat can be used in protease inhibitor-naïve patients but is not recommended for protease inhibitor-experienced patients.
